name: Japan
dek: Tokyo's 1991–2020 normal. Not a national average. Sapporo and Naha are other files, and they are not this table.
paragraphs: The table is Tokyo, WMO 47662, height 25.2 m, position 35°41′30″N, 139°45′0″E. Japan's submission also includes Sapporo, Osaka, Fukuoka, Naha, and others. None of those is averaged with Tokyo. Tokyo and Osaka now have their own sheets. Kyoto is not in the submission, so its sheet uses the Japan Meteorological Agency normal and says so.

Tokyo's average high runs from a cool January to a hot August, and the precipitation peaks in September and October rather than in a single summer month. The plug line lists both 50 hertz and 60 hertz because that is what the IEC country line says, and it does not assign a frequency to a city. The city sheets repeat that national line.

climate.caption: Reference station: Tokyo, WMO 47662. Not a national average.
climate.note: World Meteorological Organization 1991–2020 climatological standard normals, distributed by NOAA NCEI. Submitted for Japan.

plugs.label: Plugs and voltage
plugs.value: Type A and B, 100 V, 50 and 60 Hz
plugs.detail: The IEC world-plugs list shows Japan at 100 volts, with 50 hertz and 60 hertz, and plug types A and B. The country line does not say which frequency belongs to which city, so this sheet does not pick one.

driving.label: Driving side
driving.detail: The Japanese Law Translation database's English text of the Road Traffic Act says, in Article 17(4), that a vehicle must proceed along the part of the road to the left of the center. Article 18(1) says a motor vehicle that is not on a road with vehicle traffic lanes must proceed down the left side of the road, except when passing, when moving toward the center or the right edge under other articles, or when road conditions compel it.
driving.sourceTitle: Road Traffic Act, Articles 17 and 18, Japanese Law Translation

tipping.label: Tipping
tipping.detail: The Japan National Tourism Organization says it is not common to tip for bars, cafes, restaurants, taxis, and hotels. It describes a separate custom, kokorozuke, and says a private guide or interpreter who is used to overseas practice may accept a tip, which is not expected and, if offered, is put in an envelope.

water.label: Tap water
water.detail: CDC's traveler page for Japan, last reviewed 25 August 2026, does not say whether tap water is safe or unsafe. It says food and water standards around the world vary based on the destination, that standards may also differ within a country, and that risk may change depending on the activity. It points readers to CDC's food and water precautions. This page does not turn that into medical advice.

currency.label: Currency
currency.detail: ISO 4217 lists the currency name Yen and the code JPY for Japan.

timeZone.label: Time zone
timeZone.detail: IANA's zone1970.tab lists Japan on Asia/Tokyo, and Japan has only that one row. The comment on the row names Eyre Bird Observatory. The file's header says a comment is useful only for a country that has more than one zone. The comment is not a description of Japan, and it is not printed as one.

entry.publisher: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Japan
entry.note: The foreign ministry's visa page. We do not restate a visa rule.

bestTime.intro: Month by month for Tokyo, built from the station table above and two Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) records: the cherry-blossom dates observed at Tokyo and the rainy-season (tsuyu) dates for the Kantō-Kōshin region, which includes Tokyo. The JMA normals are 1991–2020 averages. They are a typical year, not a forecast. Sapporo, Osaka, Kyoto and Naha keep different calendars; the Kyoto, Osaka and Tokyo sheets have their own tables.

months.note: Average high 9.8 °C, low 1.2 °C, 59.7 mm. The coldest month in the Tokyo table.
Average high 10.9 °C, low 2.1 °C, 56.5 mm. The driest month in the table.

Average high 14.2 °C, low 5 °C, 116 mm. JMA's normal date for the first cherry blossoms at Tokyo is 24 March, and the normal full-bloom date is 31 March. Observed first-flowering dates at Tokyo were 14 March to 29 March in 2021–2026; in 2026 the trees flowered on 19 March and reached full bloom on 28 March.
Average high 19.4 °C, low 9.8 °C, 133.7 mm. Tokyo's observed full-bloom date fell in April in one year of 2021–2026 (4 April 2024); in the other years it was in March.
Average high 23.6 °C, low 14.6 °C, 139.7 mm. The month before the rainy season in a normal year.
Average high 26.1 °C, low 18.5 °C, 167.8 mm. JMA's normal start of the Kantō-Kōshin rainy season is about 7 June. In 2026 JMA puts it at about 2 June; in 2025 at about 22 May.
Average high 29.9 °C, low 22.4 °C, 156.2 mm. JMA's normal end of the Kantō-Kōshin rainy season is about 19 July, which is also the 2026 date.
Average high 31.3 °C, low 23.5 °C, 154.7 mm. The hottest month in the table, with the highest average high and the highest average low.
Average high 27.5 °C, low 20.3 °C, 224.9 mm. One of the two wettest months in the table.
Average high 22 °C, low 14.8 °C, 234.8 mm. The wettest month in the Tokyo table.
Average high 16.7 °C, low 8.8 °C, 96.3 mm. Rainfall drops by more than half from October.
